newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-TULIO SCORES FOUR GOALS AS BOTAFOGO WIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TULIO SCORES FOUR GOALS AS BOTAFOGO WIN.

text.p: Brazilian striker Tulio ended his goal drought in style by scoring four times as Botafogo hammered Bragantino 5-0 in the Brazilian championship at the weekend despite having two players sent off.
Unbeaten Palmeiras returned to the top of the table but needed a controversial last-gasp penalty to beat Sao Paulo, who had three players shown the red card.
Tulio, scorer of 50 goals for his club last year, had not got on the scoresheet for four matches until Sunday's encounter.
He ended the barren spell in the 25th minute, turning inside two defenders and scoring with a shot which sneaked in at the near post.
The second came from a penalty just before halftime and the other two in a three minute spell during the second half, making him top scorer in the competition with 10 goals.

Botafogo, who won for the third game in a row and moved within one point of the top eight, had defender Moises and midfielder Franca dismissed near the end along with Bragantino's Rubens, all for second bookable offences.
Sao Paulo's defeat led to renewed protests against coach Carlos Alberto Parreira with fans once again chanting the name of Tele Santana, who abandoned the job earlier this year due to ill-health.
Colombian international Freddy Rincon gave Palmeiras a first half lead before his compatriot Victor Hugo Aristizabal equalised with a bicycle kick.
In the last minute, Djalminha scored his ninth goal of the competition from a penalty controversially awarded after a Palmeiras forward appeared to have his shirt pulled.
Sao Paulo had midfielder Axel and defender Pedro Luis both sent off for crude tackles while Sao Paulo's Djair and Fernando Diniz of Palmeiras were sent off for fighting at the end.
The top eight in the 24-team tournament qualify for the quarter-finals.
Guarani, unbeaten for eight games, lost top place after losing 1-0 away to Sport Recife and dropped to third.
